reason: The passage presents Yahweh responding compassionately to the Israelites' suffering in Egypt, not complaining about the people. God states 'The cry of the children of Israel has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression that Egypt is oppressing them with' (וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֛ה צַעֲקַ֥ת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣אָה אֵלָ֑י וְגַם־ רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ הַלַּ֔חַץ). This demonstrates God acknowledging their distress and moving to action through Moses' mission, not expressing discontent with the people themselves. A divine complaint would involve criticism of Israel's behavior or unfaithfulness, which does not appear in this context.
